Munich. {{ cite web |url=http://www.ipni.org:80/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=426915-1 |title=Plant Name Details for ''Zerna sterilis'' |quote=Remarks: Specific epithet not associated with genus name. |work=IPNI |access-date=August 9, 2010}} }} '''''Bromus sterilis''''' is an [[Annual plant|annual]] or [[Biennial plant|biennial]] species of [[Bromus|bromegrass]] known as '''barren brome''', '''poverty brome''', and '''sterile brome'''. == Description == This is an [[Annual plant|annual]] or [[Biennial plant|biennial]] grass ranging from about 20 to 90 centimeters in maximum height. Leaf blades are 2–6 mm wide and 6–25 cm long with short, soft hair.Edgar E. & Connor H.E. 2000. Flora of New Zealand, Vol. V, Grasses. P. 368. The [[inflorescence]] is a spreading [[panicle]] with the lower parts drooping more than the upper. The [[spikelet]] is up to 6 cm long. The leaves are rough and hairy, green to purplish in colour. The [[ligule]] is pointed, toothed, 2 to 4 mm long.[http://www.bsbi.org.uk/identification.html BSBI Description] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717004923/http://www.bsbi.org.uk/identification.html |date=2011-07-17 }} retrieved 10 December 2010. [[File:Bromus sterilis (Ruderal-Trespe) IMG 0488.JPG|200px|thumbnail|Ligule is pointed]] The panicles are loose, open and nodding. The spikelets are 4 to 6 cm long, with [[Awn (botany)|awns]], producing 4 to 10 flowers.Grasses by C E Hubbard, 1978, published by Penguin books == Distribution == It can be found between sea level and 400 metres, along roadsides, hedge bottoms, and is a common weed of waste ground and gardens. This [[grass]] is native to: *northern [[Africa]] ([[Algeria]], [[Morocco]], and [[Tunisia]]); *western and middle [[Asia]] ([[Afghanistan]], [[Cyprus]], [[Iran]], [[Iraq]], [[Israel]], [[Jordan]], [[Lebanon]], [[Syria]], [[Turkey]], [[Turkmenistan]], and [[Uzbekistan]]); the [[Caucasus]] ([[Armenia]], [[Azerbaijan]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], and the [[Russian Federation]] in [[Ciscaucasia]] and [[Dagestan]]); *[[Europe]] ([[Albania]], [[Austria]], [[Belarus]], [[Belgium]], [[Bulgaria]], the [[Czech Republic]], [[Denmark]], [[France]], including [[Corsica]], [[Germany]], [[Greece]], including [[Crete]], [[Hungary]], [[Ireland]], [[Italy]], including [[Sardinia]] and [[Sicily]], [[Moldova]], the [[Netherlands]], [[Norway]], [[Poland]], [[Portugal]], [[Romania]], [[Spain]], including the [[Balearic Islands]], [[Sweden]], [[Switzerland]], [[Ukraine]], the [[United Kingdom]], and the former [[Yugoslavia]]n states). == Invasive plant species == It is well known in many parts of the world where it has become an [[introduced species]].
